texts.error.old_asound: This ASOUND.SAM is the original floppy's AdLib driver, an older build than the one OpenSamurai's AdLib is rebuilt from (the download's, %1 bytes, dated 1-10-94). Add that one, or choose another sound.
texts.error.save_unreadable: The project's saved game %1 could not be read.
texts.firmware.asound_sam: It must be the download's file (dated 1-10-94), whichever release is played. OpenSamurai's AdLib sound is built from it, and the floppy's older driver is refused.
texts.firmware.data_file.about: %1, a file of Sword of the Samurai 445.03 (MicroProse, 1989, DOS), from %2. It holds %3. You have to supply it, because this package includes none of the game's files. A modified file of your own can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.mt32.about: %1 is not one of the game's files. It is %2. You have to supply it when the sound device is the Roland, because this package includes none of it. Another MT-32 ROM that Munt knows can be used in its place, and the project then records its hash.
texts.firmware.start_exe: The floppy and the download have different builds of this file. The Release setting says which one the wizard looks for, and both play the same game.
texts.firmware.what.duel_cat: the backgrounds and fighters of the duels
texts.firmware.what.egraphic_mel: the drawing code of the melees, which use the EGA graphics mode
texts.firmware.what.misc_exe: the keyboard and joystick routines that every program of the game uses
texts.firmware.what.mt32_control_rom: the control ROM of the Roland MT-32, version 1.07, dumped from a unit of the first generation, which is the sound the game was made for
texts.firmware.what.mt32_pcm_rom: the PCM ROM of the Roland MT-32, which is the same in every MT-32
texts.firmware.what.nsound_sam: the silent sound driver, which the programs load whichever sound device is chosen
texts.firmware.what.rp_cat: the pictures of the role-playing part and the travel maps of the provinces
texts.firmware.what.rp_exe: the role-playing part of the game
texts.firmware.what.start_cat: the title pictures and the data of the windows and the political map
texts.firmware.what.start_exe: the title, the career choices and character creation
texts.property.samurai_name: The player's name, as character creation took it
texts.property.samurai_wounded: The player carries a wound (a melee into a duel, and back to the role-playing game)
texts.release.rel_download: the download sold on Steam and GOG.com
texts.setting.clock_start.about: The PC's date and time when the game starts, written as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. The clock then advances with the frames. The game reads it as the time, for example for how long a prompt waits and when an encounter on the road can happen. A movie records the start time it ran with.
texts.setting.random_seed.about: The starting number for all of the game's random numbers: the crest question, the characters, the encounters, and the opponents in duels, melees and battles. The DOS programs took their random numbers from the clock. OpenSamurai takes all of them from this one number. It can be any 64-bit number, in decimal or in hexadecimal after 0x, in the same form OpenSamurai's own program takes it (OPENSAMURAI_SEED). A number that program printed gives the same random numbers here. A movie records the number it ran with.
texts.setting.release.about: Which release of Sword of the Samurai 445.03 the project's files come from: the original floppy (the one the published speedrun uses) or the download sold on Steam and GOG.com. Both are the same game. Only START.EXE (whose code OpenSamurai does not run) and the AdLib driver differ.
texts.setting.skip_title.about: Starts the game with its /NT option. The title sequence is left out and the game starts at the copy-protection question.
texts.setting.sound.about: The sound device the game is set up for: the Roland MT-32 (the default), the AdLib, the IBM PC speaker, the Tandy, or none. The AdLib needs the download's ASOUND.SAM, because OpenSamurai's AdLib sound is built from it and the floppy has an older driver. The Roland needs RSOUND.SAM and the two ROMs of an MT-32 (version 1.07, the first generation, which the game was made for). The project supplies them as firmware. With the PC speaker the title sequence runs slower, as it did originally.
texts.slot.savedgame.help: A TALLTALE.DAT file, the game's own saved game. The game writes one when Alt+S is pressed at the Home Option scroll, and 'Restore Saved Game' in the career choices loads it. The game keeps its own saves in the machine's memory and never changes this file.
